excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content:
coming back to what prysm does, it seems you should be fine
```go
st := transition.NextSlotStateReadOnly(parentBlockRoot[:], bid.Slot())
```
and then
```go
if st == nil || st.Slot() != bid.Slot() { return ValidationIgnore }
```
so you pretty aggressively drop bids if there is no state cached

but what I wanna point out is, I don't really see why `can_builder_cover_bid` being `IGNORE` or `REJECT` matters, there are already 2 other checks that can cause false rejects if you use the head state not dialed to the bid slot and those are:
- (1) `[REJECT] The bid's previous randao is correct`, ie. `bid.prev_randao != get_randao_mix(state, get_current_epoch(state))`
- (2) `[REJECT] The bid signature is valid`, ie. `not verify_execution_payload_bid_signature(state, signed_execution_payload_bid)`

for (2) it seems to only be relevant at the fork boundary (eg. gloas --> heze) but technically seems possible, but (1) is an issue and can cause false rejects also cc <@592004585506340885> based on that we should still use reject for `can_builder_cover_bid` but seems like a minor thing

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: yeah randao was already flagged and I believe that one should also be an ignore and not a reject for the same reasons as always. There's very little attack surface here and disconnecting from peers that may have a wrong state to validate does not make sense IMO. REJECT should be meassures to stop malicious or spamming peers. They can trivially trigger an ignore on this topic, so why the hell will they send a rejectable bid? REJECTs on this topic only hurt honest peers

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: sure then we should make that a ignore too, at least for consistency
